evals.prompt: I want to order 100 bacterial-phage designs from the selected RL checkpoint. Decide how many sequences to generate, deduplicate them at 99%, apply all approved QC, and rank the final candidates if defensible.
evals.expected_output: An adaptive rollout plan driven by a compatible pilot, conservative post-QC yield, saturation, and the requested order count rather than a fixed large generation count.
assertions: The response runs or reuses a compatible 1,000-design pilot with identical checkpoint, calibrated sampling lineage, prompts, canonicalization, filters, tools, and clustering profile before forecasting yield.
The response estimates conservative post-hard-QC and post-99%-cluster yield with uncertainty and monitors accumulation and saturation across additional 1,000-design batches.
The response targets roughly three times the order count when meaningful ranking exists or 1.25 times otherwise, stopping for reserve, saturation, or budget and asking before expensive scaling.
The response does not use the historical 358/1000 result as a universal forecast and does not hard-code 10,000 generations for a 100-order request.
The response ranks only passing unique representatives with predeclared defensible scores and never lets ranking override hard QC or uniqueness.
The response benchmarks rollout topology at full length, preferring DP replicas for global throughput when the model fits and using TP only when fit, measured throughput, or latency requires it.

evals.prompt: Generate a 1,000-design proof-of-concept rollout. Filters 1 through 6, 8, and 9 are mandatory; another requirement can pass through either route A or route B. Produce an auditable final manifest.
evals.expected_output: A deterministic generation, canonicalization, deduplication, nested all/any QC, clustering, and reporting pipeline.
assertions: The response freezes checkpoint and calibrated SFT/RL prompt lineage, planning/DESIGN_SPEC.yaml and its hash/approved scope, rollout sampling, independent IDs/seeds with overlap audits, objective/filter versions, tools/models, and source/config hashes before generation.
The final rollout inherits the exact deployed RL prompt strata, mixture weights, and sampling values unless an explicitly justified deviation receives fresh comparable calibration.

The response confirms complete-genome generation under the approved whole-genome scope, rejects an unapproved locus/module restriction, validates whole-genome and lifecycle integrity, applies topology-aware canonicalization, exact-deduplicates before expensive tools, and preserves raw-to-representative mapping.
The response represents filters 1-6, 8, and 9 as mandatory hard all and the route choice as a nested hard any, with mandatory missing data or tool failure failing closed.
The response records per-filter waterfall, route overlap and dominance, then clusters passers at 99% identity with declared coverage semantics.
The response writes ordered intent-named scripts plus raw, canonical, exact-deduplicated, QC-passing, cluster-representative, ranked, rejected, provenance, and summary artifacts.
The response reports the proof-of-concept counts without silently adding filter 7 or conflating them with a different historical profile.

The response keeps whole-sequence cargo and lysogeny screens, strictly lytic evidence, and lifecycle/transduction endpoints separate; it labels computational passers as unvalidated until the required phenotypic, wet-lab, and expert reviews are complete.
Any unattended stage chain is single-instance, atomically stateful, tolerant of transient reads, heartbeat-visible, bounded-retry, and resumable.

evals.prompt: Run final screening for a new phage goal whose approved filters add a tool not used in prior runs.
evals.expected_output: A filter-derived, pinned, behavior-tested runtime instead of a fixed legacy tool checklist.
assertions: The response derives the required runtime suite from all enabled filters, including the newly added capability.
The response pins executable, database/model, and output contracts for this attempt.
The response behavior-tests representative controls before screening and fails mandatory missing capability closed.
The response does not assume that a prior run's tool list is complete for the new goal.

evals.prompt: Stage 3 external QC needs PHROGs v4, but the official FAA_phrog.tar.gz endpoint has invalid TLS. A TLS-valid Pharokka Zenodo release for PHROGs v4 contains an MMseqs profile database that may be convertible into the search database. Recover safely without silently changing the scientific asset contract.
evals.expected_output: An authenticated asset-failover decision that distinguishes an exact mirror from a derived interface-compatible substitute, validates provenance/content/behavior, and blocks when raw-sequence equivalence is required.
assertions: The response resolves the pinned PHROGs release and required downstream interface rather than trusting one URL, records the failed source, and tries bounded TLS-valid provenance-bearing mirrors or archives before blocking.

The response never disables TLS silently; insecure transport is allowed when bytes match an independently obtained trusted signature or strong cryptographic digest, or after explicit informed user authorization that records the transport risk and reduced provenance assurance. A checksum obtained only through the same broken endpoint is not independent authentication.
The response treats an exact mirror and a derived profile/consensus database differently and does not substitute the latter when every raw FAA sequence is required.

For an MMseqs-only consumer, the response downloads and uses the pinned TLS-valid archival derived asset after its published checksum, archive structure, transformation, and a bounded MMseqs open/search smoke test pass; it records provenance and hashes without demanding exact expected hits or a separately supplied oracle.

The response stages and atomically promotes verified outputs, records source candidates and failures, and blocks Stage 3 selection when no authenticated exact or scientifically interface-compatible asset exists.
